subject.title: Add retry logic to OAuth token refresh

question: Which provider errors should the shared OAuth manager retry, and what retry budget is acceptable while concurrent callers wait on the refresh lock?
rationale: The answer establishes cross-provider authentication behavior and latency rather than a mechanical implementation detail; the closed proposals retried all thrown errors and did not settle that contract.

options.title: Retry classified transient failures
options.body: Define a small shared classifier for network, timeout, and selected retryable upstream failures, then use bounded retry with a lock-aware total latency budget.

options.title: Keep single-shot refresh
options.body: Retain the existing timeout and fallback behavior if predictable auth latency is more important than recovering transient upstream failures.

options.title: Retry only in specific provider owners
options.body: Keep the shared manager single-shot and let providers with reliable error contracts opt into their own retry behavior.

recommendation.title: Retry classified transient failures
recommendation.body: Define a small shared classifier for network, timeout, and selected retryable upstream failures, then use bounded retry with a lock-aware total latency budget.

likelyOwner.reason: The OAuth-manager refactor history makes this person the clearest available owner for the shared-policy choice.
